newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA BEAT NORWAY TO GIVE VENABLES DREAM START.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AUSTRALIA BEAT NORWAY TO GIVE VENABLES DREAM START.

text.p: Hosts Australia won a four-nations tournament by beating Norway 1-0 on Saturday to provide Terry Venables with a dream start in his new job as national coach.
Left back Robbie Hooker scored the only goal in the 72nd minute to secure Australia's third win in seven days for a maximum haul of nine points.

"We can't get carried away because we've got a long way to go but it's a very good sign, I'm very encouraged," said former England coach Venables, whose side defeated New Zealand and South Korea in their previous matches in the tournament.
In the earlier match at the Sydney Football Stadium, South Korea came back from a goal down to beat New Zealand 3-1 and claim second place on the table with six points from three games.
Australia organised the series as part of their preparations for the Oceania qualifying group matches later this year for the 1998 World Cup in France.
"In the second half Norway had to come and get the ball, so they stretched their team... and I thought in the last 15 minutes they got tired," Venables said.

The former Barcelona and Tottenham Hotspur coach, who left his job with England after guiding them to the semifinals of last year's European championship, signed an 18-month contract to lead Australia's qualifying campaign.
New Zealand, who finished without a point from three games, led 1-0 at half time through a goal from striker Vaughan Coveny but the South Koreans scored three times in the final 14 minutes.
Forward Park Kun Ha equalised in the 77th minute with substitute Go Jong Su scoring in the 83rd minute and setting up Yoo Sang Chui for the third.
Norway finished with three points from three games.
